question.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-y=2 \\ 2x+3y=1.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we construct ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$
